official_baseline_claims.claim: Upstream provides persistent structural graph queries, caller/callee tracing and compact, paginated outputs to reduce exploratory source loading. It is a structural backend, with the MCP client supplying the language model.

The release already contains compact output and response budgeting; its release-note tokenizer comparison concerns a serialized tools/list fixture, not a whole agent session or this native adaptation.

Upstream explicitly separates answer quality, graph performance and model-token savings. Its measurement guide requires paired runs on the same repository revision, questions, model, prompt, budget and session policy; graph query counters cannot reveal final model consumption.

limitations.text: search_graph, query_graph and trace_path expose no automatic 0.5 confidence floor. trace_path's include_evidence defaults to false and reveals resolver class/confidence when enabled; the implementation explicitly presents this as an opt-in for judging edge trust. The same behavior remains in current main, so a 0.5 acceptance cutoff is a caller policy rather than an upstream default or a recommendation in these schemas.

The pinned pipeline stores confidence and strategy on CALLS edges. Its PC_SVC_PATTERN_CONF=0.5 constant assigns confidence to inferred service-pattern edges when registry resolution is empty; it does not prescribe dropping all edges below 0.5.

Graph absence is not proof of complete coverage, and output budgets are deterministic byte-based sizing hints rather than tokenizer-exact limits. Callers must inspect coverage and pagination rather than assuming an empty or bounded response is an exhaustive source result.

Automatic indexing is off by default, but automatic watching and the watcher subsystem default to on. A registered MCP server therefore does not imply an indexed repository, and disabling indexing alone does not disable all background coordination.

Retained upstream issue evidence reports that the v0.11.0 Claude SubagentStart installer emits an unsupported separate args field; the maintainer confirmed that generated shape. This is an installer-path defect, not a demonstrated failure of manually registered MCP queries.

Retained upstream issue evidence and maintainer confirmation identify a Codex installer preservation gap: unrelated tables inside CBM's managed markers can be removed on rewrite. Re-running the full installer is not a justified repair for a missing manually managed registration.

The catalog selects the official v0.11.0 codebase-memory-mcp-linux-amd64.tar.gz release archive and recorded checksum, then invokes the installed binary directly rather than running its all-client installer (recipes/README.md:88). The observed Codex launcher is ${ECO_ROOT}/bin/codebase-memory-mcp. Although manifests/stack.json:272 labels the component core, it appears in no adoption profile and neither platform pins file, so automated bootstrap does not install it on a new host; the handbook explicitly records this gap and the absence of a documented Mac install in that recipe (adoption/manifest.json:191; adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json; adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json; docs/token-session-handbook.md:211).
native_adaptation.claude_wiring: The scope decision describes an existing Claude user-scope server that the Codex setup mirrors (docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md:63). Portable adoption/mcp/claude-user.json registers only ai-memory and Serena; adoption/templates/claude.settings.template.json adds no CBM registration or hooks, and examples/claude-mcp.json.example also has no CBM entry. The explicit bridge recipe is examples/mcporter.json.example:16 plus recipes/README.md:585. None of the six shipped examples/claude-native/agents/*.md tool lists grants either CBM MCP namespace; this includes examples/claude-native/agents/evidence-reviewer.md:4 and examples/claude-native/agents/isolated-builder.md:4, despite their Serena and jCodeMunch grants. Bash-enabled agents can still use a CLI/bridge, so the verified gap is direct native MCP access rather than the impossibility of every kind of invocation.
native_adaptation.codex_wiring: adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml:72 registers [mcp_servers.codebase-memory] at user scope with command ${ECO_ROOT}/bin/codebase-memory-mcp and no arguments. Live read-only `codex mcp list --json` and `codex mcp get codebase-memory --json` confirm the entry; a neutral-directory merged list also contains it, so availability does not depend on the main checkout's untracked .codex/config.toml. This verifies configuration availability, not a newly executed indexing or graph-query result (docs/token-session-handbook.md:67; docs/token-session-handbook.md:214).
native_adaptation.lane_rule: Use the on-demand static-graph lane with explicit project/node identifiers, bounded search_graph/trace_path requests and original-source checks (docs/token-session-handbook.md:139). The recipe explicitly indexes selected code in fast mode, uses CBM_ALLOWED_ROOT in the bridge example and reindexes after relevant edits; persistence:false avoids a repository snapshot but does not make the account database ephemeral (recipes/README.md:585; examples/mcporter.json.example:16).

deviations_from_upstream.what: The Q3 confidence cutoff is local policy, not an upstream default or a documented upstream threshold in the reviewed query/trace contracts. Upstream supports trace_path(include_evidence=true), but leaves it false by default and applies no general 0.5 confidence floor (https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/v0.11.0/src/mcp/mcp.c#L483-L558; https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/v0.11.0/src/mcp/mcp.c#L9004-L9009). The source's service-pattern 0.5 constant is an assigned score, not a filter (https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/v0.11.0/src/pipeline/pass_calls.c#L15-L17).
deviations_from_upstream.why: The assembled card's Q3 fixture contains weak inferred edges and missed callers through a try/except relative import. Confidence filtering can reject a weak false positive; it cannot restore callers the index never resolved, so a smaller graph payload is not complete enumeration.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Document the 0.5 cutoff as a Q3-derived local heuristic. Read-only traversal of the matching graph yields 9 of 12 genuine direct callers; requiring confidence >= 0.5 removes two genuine callers at confidence 0.38, leaving 7 of 12, and also removes valid two-hop paths through freshness_propose.apply. A 0.5 cutoff is not established as a suitable fix merely because it removes the one demonstrated 0.07 false positive. Qualify any cutoff against known callers before recommending it; do not substitute another untested threshold. Request trace evidence, filter edge confidence explicitly in query/output handling where available only after that qualification, retain coverage caveats, and cross-check exact enumeration with Serena and original source. Keep low-confidence candidates available for source or Serena cross-check rather than silently dropping them. Do not pass include_evidence as though it were a search_graph or query_graph parameter.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The manifest's core label does not match an automated fresh-host install path: no adoption profile or platform pin selects CBM, despite the user MCP template naming its executable (manifests/stack.json:272; adoption/manifest.json:191; adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json; adoption/pins-macos-arm64.json; adoption/templates/codex.config.template.toml:72; docs/token-session-handbook.md:211).
deviations_from_upstream.why: Catalog membership and server registration have been maintained separately from bootstrap coverage. An already installed host can work while a new adopter receives a server entry for an absent binary.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Either add qualified platform pins and explicit profile selection, or label the component as manual adoption and gate its server registration on installation. Keep unsupported platform coverage explicit.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The shipped Claude profile supplies neither a CBM server entry nor direct CBM grants to its agents, unlike upstream's documented graph-agent integration (adoption/mcp/claude-user.json; examples/claude-native/agents/evidence-reviewer.md:4; examples/claude-native/agents/isolated-builder.md:4; https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/blob/v0.11.0/README.md#L493-L585).
deviations_from_upstream.why: A host-level registration cannot satisfy a shipped agent's explicit tool allowlist. Manual CLI/bridge use remains possible in Bash-enabled agents, but that is a separate route and does not repair direct MCP availability.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: For projects adopting the graph lane, provide explicit server registration and narrow read-only graph-tool grants to the intended agents, then verify a useful call from those agents. Do not assume the current examples inherit every host MCP tool.

deviations_from_upstream.what: The adaptation intentionally uses manual direct-MCP/bridge setup and explicit indexing rather than upstream's broad installer, activation pointers and generated hooks (recipes/README.md:88; recipes/README.md:585; docs/decisions/2026-09-25-codex-mcp-scope.md:74). The inspected card records that the main checkout was not indexed for the retained adaptation; user-scope registration alone does not fix that.
deviations_from_upstream.why: The catalog requires bounded project adoption and preserves existing client configuration. This also avoids the installer paths implicated by the retained upstream hook and Codex configuration-preservation reports (https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/issues/2239; https://github.com/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/issues/2228). Upstream auto_index=false is itself the default, so keeping it off is not a departure from that default.
deviations_from_upstream.fix: Explicitly index an opted-in repository and verify freshness/coverage before graph work. Keep hook installation separate from MCP availability and qualify generated client configuration before enabling it.

final_verdict.summary: Installed v0.11.0 matches the latest release and supports the chosen explicit-index graph workflow, but portable installation and Claude agent access remain incomplete. The historical verified task artifacts were 22,445→19,635 tokens for Claude (12.5%) and 22,445→16,109 for Codex (28.2%), eligible only for those checked caller-retrieval tasks, not provider savings (evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-ultracode-20260925/receipt.json; evidence/artifacts/token-e2e-codex-20260926/receipt.json). The newer MCPorter comparisons of 56,274→865 (98.5%) and 56,274→1,410 (97.5%) are not clean complete-answer savings: graph-only recall is 4/7, while search_code restores 7/7 recall but includes one false positive (../rr/codebase-memory-mcp/records.json#codebase-memory-mcp:compare-mcp-plan; #codebase-memory-mcp:compare-mcp-plan-plus-search-code). In the fixed 36-hour scan, 9/1,010 Ultracode workflow children (0.89%) and 1/301 Codex workers (0.33%) invoked it, with 0/22 children carrying TOKEN LANES invoking it; these are invocation observations, not success rates (invoke_by_tool.json). Next, qualify explicit indexing, source-validated fallback and narrow Claude grants, preserve low-confidence candidates for verification, and measure the intended native worker path without combining artifact counts with counters or provider usage.
